title: A durable, implantable artificial kidney

concept.text: A durable, implantable artificial kidney would be a manufactured device placed inside the body that continuously provides sufficient kidney replacement to sustain a person with kidney failure. It would remove appropriate wastes and excess water while maintaining fluid and electrolyte balance, with reliable operation over long periods. The defining advance is an integrated replacement system; an isolated blood filter or a short-lived compartment of kidney cells would demonstrate only part of that capability.

One proposed route combines a hemofilter with a bioreactor containing living renal cells. The filter produces an ultrafiltrate from blood, and the cell compartment would process that fluid, recovering needed water and sodium while directing remaining waste toward the bladder. Silicon nanopore membranes are intended to support exchange while protecting the cells from immune attack. This bioartificial architecture illustrates the concept, but the innovation ultimately depends on sustained replacement function and safety rather than on any single component design.

significance.text: If achieved, sustained kidney replacement from a fully implanted manufactured system would provide a fundamentally different treatment option for kidney failure. A recipient could obtain continuous replacement without recurring maintenance dialysis sessions or a donor kidney. This would address two major constraints motivating the research: the burden and incomplete functional replacement of hemodialysis, and the limited availability of transplant organs.

Conditional impact synthesis: successful deployment could reduce dependence on donor supply and dialysis infrastructure, but the scale of that effect would depend on manufacturing capacity, affordability, surgical access, device durability and adoption. An implant could also shift care toward implantation, monitoring, maintenance and eventual replacement. Better quality of life, improved clinical outcomes and lower total costs are possibilities to test, rather than automatic consequences of putting treatment inside the body.

The analogy to a natural kidney has important limits. Demonstrating filtration, tubular processing or dialysis independence would not by itself establish that the implant reproduces every renal function. Endocrine sufficiency and the need for continuing medicines or other supplementation would require separate evaluation. The supplied component study does not establish complete physiological replacement or clinical superiority.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central capability still to be established by the supplied evidence is durable integration: coupling filtration to sufficient downstream fluid processing and waste excretion in one implanted system. A filter must deliver an appropriate ultrafiltrate, and the processing compartment must recover needed substances and water at rates sufficient for kidney replacement. Cell survival or expression of renal genes alone cannot establish that the combined system provides adequate transport, clearance or life support.

Long-term operation also requires a safe interface with blood and surrounding tissues. Concrete barriers include thrombosis, infection, loss of device integrity and sustained compatibility of the membranes and vascular connections. For a living-cell design, enough cells must remain viable and functionally active while being protected from immune attack. The 2023 paper identifies increased cell numbers, longer implantation periods and testing in animals with reduced renal function as future steps; its short implants do not establish that these requirements can be maintained for years.

Engineering synthesis: a practical implant would also need reproducible manufacture, consistent functional performance, monitoring that detects deterioration, and workable procedures for maintenance or replacement. Its operating limits would need definition, including how it handles changing fluid and electrolyte demands and which functions require supplementation. These are requirements for translating a successful prototype into durable treatment, not capabilities demonstrated in the supplied study.

current_state.text: Kim and colleagues reported a bioreactor component study in Nature Communications on August 29, 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-39888-2. They implanted a human renal-cell bioreactor in five healthy female adolescent Yucatan minipigs: three implants lasted three days and two lasted seven days. The experiment demonstrated short-term feasibility of an implanted cell compartment. It did not test an integrated hemofilter–bioreactor system providing life-sustaining replacement in animals with kidney failure.

The animals received no immunosuppression and no ongoing systemic anticoagulation. They did receive aspirin and clopidogrel through device retrieval, as well as an intraoperative intravenous heparin dose of 100 units/kg before vessel occlusion. This distinction matters: the study supports short-term implantation under that specific drug regimen, rather than implantation with no antithrombotic treatment or no exposure to anticoagulants.

Functional evidence principally concerned cell viability and gene-expression surrogates. These observations support further development, but they do not establish replacement-level transport or clearance. The healthy animals retained their own kidney function, so their survival cannot demonstrate that the bioreactor could sustain a recipient with kidney failure. Longer implantation, functional transport testing, greater cell capacity and integration remained future work in the paper.

Evidence boundary: the supplied review reports complete text extraction across the article's 11 pages, with no recorded extraction issues or truncation. Linked supplementary material was not included in that review, and its conclusions did not require inspection of figure images. The supplied evidence therefore supports this dated 2023 result within those limits. No freshness search was supplied to establish the latest state as of November 2026; that limitation does not show that subsequent advances have or have not occurred.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a fully implanted integrated system should sustain people with kidney failure without maintenance dialysis for years, with acceptable complications and quality of life. A clinical protocol would need to define those outcomes prospectively, including the handling of rescue dialysis, device revisions and treatment discontinuation. The years-long endpoint is a proposed test of durability, not an established standard or a result reported by the supplied source.
completion_criteria.label: Fully implanted system sustains years-long dialysis independence with acceptable outcomes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed functional evidence: demonstrate adequate waste removal, water balance and electrolyte regulation under clinically relevant conditions, with direct measurements of integrated performance. For a cell-based device, confirm sustained transport function as well as cell viability. Identify essential functions the implant supplies and those managed by supplementation, including any endocrine needs, so that dialysis independence is not mistaken for complete replication of a natural kidney.
completion_criteria.label: Integrated implant demonstrates adequate waste removal and fluid-electrolyte regulation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: reproduce performance across independently manufactured devices, clinical teams and a defined range of patients. Follow recipients long enough to characterize thrombosis, infection, immune injury where relevant, mechanical failures, medication requirements and replacement procedures. Assess manufacturing consistency, maintenance burden and patient-reported outcomes. Such finite studies would establish demonstrated breadth and durability within their tested populations and conditions, rather than literal universality or unlimited device life.
completion_criteria.label: Performance reproduces across independently manufactured devices, clinical teams and patients

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: NEP-01, “Regrow functional nephrons inside an adult human kidney,” and NEP-02, “Rebuild function in scarred kidneys by reversing established fibrosis,” seek to restore the patient's existing kidneys. NEP-04 instead supplies replacement through an implanted manufactured system. Living renal cells could contribute to either approach, but regeneration within native tissue and operation inside a device remain distinct capabilities.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-03, “Manufacture transplantable human kidneys from cells,” shares the goal of creating replacement capacity without relying on conventional donor supply. Its defining product is a transplantable human kidney, whereas NEP-04 is an artificial or bioartificial device that may combine engineered membranes with cells. NEP-06, “An effectively unlimited supply of durable animal-donor kidneys,” pursues another replacement route through animal organs. Each route has different requirements for production, implantation, compatibility and durability.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-05, “Kidney replacement that is portable and affordable at global scale,” overlaps with the freedom from recurring facility-based treatment that an implant might offer. Its defining requirements are portability, affordability and broad access; NEP-04 specifically requires durable implantation. An implant could be expensive or difficult to maintain, while a portable replacement system could remain outside the body. Neither concept's success automatically establishes the other.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-07, “Reliably induce donor-specific tolerance in kidney recipients,” concerns acceptance of donor tissue. It overlaps with the immune-protection challenge of a cell-containing artificial kidney, but membrane-based protection of cells inside a device is distinct from inducing donor-specific immune tolerance. The bioreactor's short-term use without immunosuppression does not demonstrate transplantation tolerance.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-08, “A root-cause, durable treatment for ADPKD,” NEP-09, “Durable reversal of diabetic kidney disease,” and NEP-10, “Broad prevention of severe acute kidney injury,” aim to treat underlying disease or prevent kidney damage. Their success could reduce the need for replacement. NEP-04 addresses loss of kidney function after replacement becomes necessary; providing that function does not itself demonstrate treatment of those underlying causes.

change_log.reason: The original wording could obscure the documented surgical anticoagulant exposure.

change_log.reason: The reviewed findings support component feasibility without establishing integrated renal replacement.

change_log.reason: The replacement capability supports the former; the latter require evidence about durability, deployment, access and clinical performance.

change_log.change: Made the proposed completion criteria explicit and added reproducibility, measurable outcomes and practical operating boundaries.
change_log.reason: The years-long human endpoint is coherent but is not a published standard; finite demonstrations establish performance only within tested conditions.

unresolved_issues: The latest development state as of November 2026 cannot be established from the supplied 2023 article and empty freshness record.
The reviewed evidence does not establish integrated replacement-level transport, dialysis independence or long-term performance in kidney failure.
Long-term cell function, immune protection, hemocompatibility, infection risk and device integrity remain unestablished by these short-duration implants.
Linked supplementary material was outside the supplied review; its potential contribution is not resolved here.
Endocrine sufficiency, supplementation needs, affordability, clinical superiority and scalable manufacture remain to be demonstrated.
The proposed human completion endpoint still requires measurable acceptance criteria, a defined patient population, follow-up duration and rules for rescue treatment or device revision.

brief.title: A lasting kidney replacement inside the body
possible: People with kidney failure could live without recurring dialysis sessions, where a machine cleans their blood, or a donor kidney. A manufactured device inside the body would continuously remove wastes and excess water while keeping water and salts in balance.
why: Treatment could take up less of a person's life. An implant would also offer a replacement option that does not depend on the limited supply of donated kidneys.

sources.who: Eun Jung Kim, Caressa Chen and colleagues
sources.showed: Human kidney cells survived inside an implanted chamber in healthy pigs and retained signs of activity. The animals received drugs to prevent blood clots, but no drugs to suppress immune rejection.
sources.quote:
Despite
implantation into a xenograft model, we ﬁnd that cells exhibit minimal
damage, and recipient cytokine levels are not suggestive of hyperacute
rejection.
sources.cited_for: A chamber containing living kidney cells can survive short implantation without immune-suppressing drugs.
sources.not_established: Cell survival and signs of activity do not establish enough waste removal or fluid processing to replace kidney function.

sources.showed: Implanted blood filters worked briefly in dogs without becoming blocked by clots. Some membranes developed microscopic fractures during longer tests.
sources.quote: In conclusion, a detailed mechanistic and materials science attention to blood–material interactions allows implanted hemofilters to resist thrombosis.
sources.cited_for: Implanted filters can use the recipient's blood pressure to drive filtration while resisting clots over short periods.
sources.not_established: The filters did not demonstrate durable operation or replacement of the kidneys.

sources.who: Melissa E Melvin, William H Fissell, Shuvo Roy and David L Brown
sources.showed: Silicon samples with a protective coating showed no attached clots under electron microscopy after four weeks in rat veins. Bare silicon had small attached clots.
sources.quote: Under scanning electron microscopy, bare silicon implants were found to have significant adherent microthrombi, while PEG-treated implants showed no evidence of thrombi.
sources.cited_for: A surface coating can reduce clot attachment to silicon exposed to blood.
sources.not_established: Material samples in veins do not establish the safety or durability of a working kidney replacement.

shown: Kim and colleagues kept human kidney cells alive in an implanted chamber in healthy pigs for up to seven days. This tested a component of a proposed system that would combine a blood filter with living cells to recover needed water and salts. The pigs retained their own kidney function.
missing: An integrated implant has yet to sustain a recipient with kidney failure by filtering blood, processing the filtered fluid and sending wastes for excretion.
Years of operation without dangerous clots, infection, immune damage or device failure remain to be demonstrated.
Consistent manufacture, detection of declining performance and workable maintenance or replacement procedures remain to be demonstrated.

milestones.label: An implant sustains years without dialysis
milestones.explanation: A fully implanted system would have to keep people with kidney failure off maintenance dialysis for years, with acceptable complications and quality of life. This would establish lasting treatment.

milestones.label: The integrated implant controls wastes, water and salts
milestones.explanation: Direct measurements would have to show sufficient waste removal and water and salt regulation, with sustained cell activity where relevant. This would establish what the implant supplies and what needs supplementation.

milestones.label: Performance holds across devices, teams and patients
milestones.explanation: Independent manufacture and different clinical teams would have to reproduce performance across a defined range of patients, with extended follow-up. This would establish reliability and practical limits beyond an initial success.

uncertain: The implant's ability to supply kidney hormone functions, and the medicines or supplements recipients would still need, remain open questions.
Human trials still need clear rules for acceptable outcomes, emergency dialysis and device revision.
Affordability, better clinical outcomes and lower total costs remain possibilities to test.

page.title: Implantable artificial kidney
page.definition: A manufactured system implanted wholly inside the body continuously removes wastes and excess water and regulates salts well enough to replace maintenance dialysis in chronic kidney failure. In one design, a blood filter produces a fluid containing water, salts and dissolved wastes. Living kidney cells return much of the filtered water to the blood, and the concentrated waste fluid drains to the bladder. Other designs use cell-free components to regulate salts and water.

goal.need: On March 31, 2025, 516,837 people in the United States were on dialysis. For the 433,396 receiving in-center hemodialysis, a usual schedule was about four hours three times a week, plus travel. Home hemodialysis offers more flexibility but still takes hours on a machine. An implant that maintained waste clearance and fluid balance could free that time for work and family, whether someone was waiting for a donor kidney or needed long-term treatment. Some recipients could still need hormone replacement.

completion.title: FDA approves an implanted artificial kidney to replace maintenance dialysis.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing approval for a fully implanted manufactured kidney system whose labelled intended use is ongoing kidney replacement in people with chronic kidney failure without maintenance dialysis. Under the device premarket approval standard, the evidence must establish reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness for that use. The approved population, conditions of use and operating duration are those in the approval and labelling.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Device Approvals and Clearances: general premarket approval standard applied to the intended use defined here.
completion.threshold_quote: sufficient valid scientific evidence that provides reasonable assurance that the device is safe and effective for its intended use or uses.
completion.basis: The developer identifies FDA approval after clinical trials as necessary for widespread use. This applies FDA's general device approval test; it does not establish which regulatory pathway FDA will assign to a cell-containing combination product. No published implant-specific human durability cut-off was found.

milestones.title: An artificial-kidney blood filter produces at least 40 L/day of filtrate without clotting.
milestones.criterion: Connect the filter to the circulation, with or without a pump. It must produce at least 40 L of filtrate per day without clotting, retain essential blood proteins such as albumin, and freely pass electrolytes and toxins that are not bound to proteins.
milestones.set_by: Kidney Health Initiative, 2018 roadmap, Table 2, page 19, and Table 3, page 22.
milestones.threshold_quote: Generates a filtrate of at least 40L/day

milestones.title: An artificial-kidney filter functions in a full-scale animal model with residual kidney function.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate blood filtration by the candidate filter in a full-scale animal model that retains native kidney function. The need for the study and its duration depend on the product.
milestones.set_by: Kidney Health Initiative, 2018 roadmap, Table 3, page 23; biohybrid blood-filtration target, stated in a table.
milestones.threshold_quote: full-scale animal model with residual kidney function

milestones.title: An artificial-kidney filter functions in animals with no residual kidney function.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate blood filtration by the candidate filter in an anephric animal model, with no residual native kidney function. The need for the study and its duration depend on the product.
milestones.set_by: Kidney Health Initiative, 2018 roadmap, Table 3, page 23; biohybrid blood-filtration target, stated in a table.
milestones.threshold_quote: anephric animal models without residual kidney function

milestones.title: A non-clotting artificial-kidney filter produces 40 L/day continuously for 12–24 months.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate 12–24 months of continuous performance by a size-selective filter capable of producing 40 L of filtrate per day without clotting.
milestones.set_by: Kidney Health Initiative, 2018 roadmap, Table 3, page 23; blood-filtration durability target, stated in a table.
milestones.threshold_quote: 40L/day filtrate with 12–24 months of continuous performance

milestones.title: A fully implanted artificial kidney produces initial human safety and device-function data.
milestones.criterion: Use a fully implanted artificial kidney in an authorized early feasibility study in people and obtain initial data on clinical safety and device function.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Early Feasibility Studies Program; general clinical-development stage, not an implant-specific protocol.
milestones.threshold_quote: initial clinical safety and device functionality

milestones.title: A pivotal human study evaluates an implanted artificial kidney as a dialysis replacement.
milestones.criterion: Complete a pivotal human investigation of the implanted system for its intended use as a replacement for maintenance dialysis. Evaluate safety and effectiveness against the study's prospectively specified primary endpoints.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Design Considerations for Pivotal Clinical Investigations for Medical Devices; general pivotal-study stage.
milestones.threshold_quote: A definitive study during which evidence is gathered to support the safety and effectiveness evaluation of the medical device for its intended use.

milestones.title: A prototype implant component demonstrates its intended kidney function in the laboratory.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate the component's intended function experimentally. For a hemofiltration membrane, measure fluid passage and the passage or retention of solutes during filtration of blood. Report the test conditions, including any anticoagulation.
milestones.set_by: KidneyX Artificial Kidney Prize, Phase 1, component proof-of-concept criterion applied to an implant component.
milestones.threshold_quote: component or integrated prototype solutions with demonstrated performance, including proof of concept data

milestones.title: A tubular component permits net reabsorption of 90%–95% of filtered volume outside the body.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate outside the body that the water transport and permeability of the cellular structure permit net reabsorption of 90%–95% of the volume filtered. The denominator is the volume entering from filtration.
milestones.set_by: Kidney Health Initiative, 2018 roadmap, Table 3, page 24, cellular fluid-regulation activity.
milestones.threshold_quote: net reabsorption of 90%–95% of filtered volume

milestones.title: An integrated implant prototype demonstrates blood filtration and processing of the filtrate.
milestones.criterion: Show that the connected prototype filters blood and processes the resulting fluid for excretion. In a filter–bioreactor implant, demonstrate filtration, return of fluid to the blood and delivery of the remaining fluid to the urinary tract. Record performance with the components connected.
milestones.set_by: KidneyX Artificial Kidney Prize, Phase 1, integrated prototype proof of concept, applied to the implantable system.
milestones.threshold_quote: integrated prototype solutions with demonstrated performance

not_found: Web searches of ClinicalTrials.gov, FDA sources and developer materials found no public human implant protocol specifying dialysis-independence duration, rescue-dialysis rules or numerical success limits.
No published result establishing the roadmap's 12–24-month, 40 L/day filter target was found.
The full text of the Nature Reviews Nephrology roadmap published on 6 November 2026 could not be opened.
No regulator or nephrology society position rejecting the feasibility or value of a fully implanted artificial kidney was found.

results.finding: Human renal epithelial cells shielded by the bioreactor membrane retained 88.6% viability across 3 independent experiments.
results.detail: The assay used cell culture medium, so blood anticoagulation was inapplicable.
results.quote:
Cells in the basal compartment maintained high
rates of viability (approaching 90%) (Fig.1c).

results.finding: Explanted bioreactor cells expressed aquaporin-1 at 1.05 times the in vitro control level (n = 4 biological samples).
results.detail: The authors cite the small number of encapsulated cells as a limitation on measuring volume transport. They did not collect apical filtrate.
results.quote:
Expression of aquaporin 1 (AQP1), a molecular water channel protein
present on apical and basal surfaces of renal cells, was comparable to
in vitro control cells after 3 days (Fig. 6c).

results.finding: Silicon nanopore membranes (bench sample size unreported) averaged 1.0 μl/min in saline filtration.
results.quote: Benchtop filtration rates at 103 mm Hg averaged 1.0 μl/min.

results.finding: Implanted silicon hemofilters in six dogs yielded at most 50 mL per membrane at explant.
results.detail: The dogs received intraoperative heparin and postoperative aspirin. Membrane defects were associated with greater albumin leakage.

results.finding: Implanted silicon hemofilters filtered blood in six dogs with native kidneys for up to 8 days.
results.detail: The operation left the native kidneys in place. Residual renal function was inferred from the surgical model. The study used small-scale cartridges.
results.quote: Sustained (3–8) day function of an implanted parallel-plate hemofilter with minimal anticoagulation was achieved by considering biocompatibility at the subnanometer scale of chemical interactions and the millimeter scale of blood fluid dynamics.

results.finding: Silicon nanopore membranes (sample size unreported) showed predicted hydraulic permeability and macromolecular sieving. Numerical measurements were unreported.
results.quote: Hydraulic permeability of these membranes matched predictions for laminar flow through slit pores.

results.finding: The hemofilter in one pig produced 4 μl/min of ultrafiltrate, with no thrombus observed at explant.
results.detail: The daily equivalent is calculated from the pre-connection rate. The article gives no measured 24-hour filtrate volume.
results.quote: Before connecting the bioreactor, the hemofilter was generating 4 μl per minute of clear yellowish ultrafiltrate.

results.finding: Cultured tubule cells showed active volume transport (sample size unreported). The implanted bioreactor in one pig showed an estimated 92.5% reabsorption.
results.detail: The estimate uses the pre-connection filtration rate as the denominator. The article does not give a simultaneous measurement of filtrate entering the connected bioreactor.
results.quote: After connecting the bioreactor, the effluent rate leaving the bioreactor was 0.3 μl per minute, confirming reabsorption by the tubule cells in the bioreactor.

results.finding: A small-scale implanted hemofilter in one pig produced 4 μl/min of ultrafiltrate.
results.detail: The separate report of medium-scale implants in swine gives no filtration measurements.
results.quote: Before connecting the bioreactor, the hemofilter was generating 4 μl per minute of clear yellowish ultrafiltrate.

results.finding: The connected hemofilter and bioreactor in one pig delivered effluent to the bladder at 0.3 μl/min.
results.detail: The authors measured the 4 μl/min filter output before connecting the bioreactor and the effluent rate after connection.
results.quote: After connecting the bioreactor, the effluent rate leaving the bioreactor was 0.3 μl per minute, confirming reabsorption by the tubule cells in the bioreactor.

results.finding: Five bi-culture grafts produced measurable urine with lower total protein and hematocrit than serum during 1 hour of blood perfusion.
results.detail: The circuit targeted 100 mmHg arterial pressure, with blood flow of 300–800 mL/min. Urine from endothelial-only controls was recirculated to maintain perfusate volume.
results.quote: In comparison, bi-culture BEKs with recellularized glomeruli demonstrated urine with significantly lower protein and hematocrit values relative to serum throughout the 1-hour perfusion period, indicating filtration capabilities.

results.finding: Five bi-culture grafts implanted in pigs produced mean ureteral outflow of 1.26 mL/min in acute testing.
results.detail: The reported mean corresponds to about 1.8 L/day if sustained. It reflects early sampling points across sessions, including the first session, which showed no evidence of selective filtration.
results.quote: Urine flow rates across the three implant sessions averaged 1.26 mL/min ± 1.3 for values collected at 30 min and 60 min of in vivo perfusion

results.finding: One of five bi-culture grafts tested in pigs sustained blood filtration for up to 5 hours.
results.detail: The first session showed no filtration by the study readouts. The final session used a single initial dose of heparin, and graft urine was collected separately through a ureteral cannula.
results.quote: While implant 3 only tested a single BEK, this implant extended the examination window up to 5 hours, demonstrating sustained filtration function with remarkably low (around 1%) urine hematocrit and lower urine protein levels compared to serum protein levels

results.finding: A cell-free hemofilter in one goat continuously produced filtrate for 10 days.
results.detail: The 1.5 L/day figure is a design target. Heparin was adjusted after the activated clotting time exceeded 300 seconds during the first two days.
results.quote: 10-day experimental period, and filtrate was continuously obtained.

results.finding: An implanted cell-free hemofilter in one goat yielded filtrate continuously for 10 days.
results.detail: The filter operated without an external pump. Systemic heparin was used with an activated clotting time target of approximately 250 seconds.
results.quote: 10-day experimental period, and filtrate was continuously obtained.

results.finding: The Holly filter transferred wastes from blood to dialysate in one sheep during a 72-hour study with no reported clotting.
results.detail: The release gives no numerical filtrate volume, albumin measurement or solute sieving data.
results.quote: No evidence of blood clotting, hemolysis or device leakage throughout the study period.

results.finding: The Holly filter transferred urea, creatinine and potassium to dialysate in one sheep during a 72-hour study.
results.detail: The release gives no surgical or functional information about the sheep’s native kidneys.
results.quote: Continuous waste removal with effective filtration of key toxins including urea, creatinine and potassium from blood to dialysate.

results.finding: The Holly prototype filtered blood and automatically managed fluid in one sheep over 72 hours.
results.detail: The release does not identify where the device sent the waste-bearing dialysate.
results.quote: The device demonstrated self-regulatory function, including intelligent fluid management that automatically supplied fluid when needed and removed excess fluid as required.

results.finding: The Holly filter ran continuously in one sheep for 72 hours with no reported evidence of blood clotting.
results.quote: No evidence of blood clotting, hemolysis or device leakage throughout the study period.

results.finding: In vitro imaging validated flow simulations for prototype hemofilter conduits. The laboratory sample size was unreported.
results.detail: The laboratory result concerns flow within the conduit. Aspirin use was reported for the dog study.
results.quote: Computational fluid dynamics simulations were validated by flow field imaging in vitro.

results.finding: In six aspirin-treated dogs, prototype hemofilter cartridges had no visible thrombosis at 30 days.
results.detail: Two cartridges were implanted at each channel width of 500, 750 and 1000 µm. The evidence comes from a conference poster abstract published in a journal supplement.
results.quote: The optically transparent cartridges had no visible thrombosis at any flow channel pathway size.

results.finding: Prototype hemofilter conduits in six dogs were patent on serial Doppler during a 30-day implant study.
results.detail: All dogs received acetylsalicylic acid. Doppler assessed conduit patency.
results.quote: Serial Doppler ultrasound examination verified patency of blood conduits.

results.finding: The implanted silicon nanopore hemodialyzer remained patent for 7 days in one minipig.
results.detail: The animal received aspirin and clopidogrel and an intraoperative heparin bolus. There was no ongoing systemic anticoagulation. An external pump recirculated saline at 0 mmHg transmembrane pressure to prevent ultrafiltration.
results.quote: A small-scale SNMHD was successfully implanted, remained patent for the entire 7-day study without systemic anticoagulation, and cleared uremic toxins and solutes without leakage of albumin.

results.finding: An implanted silicon nanopore hemodialyzer in one subtotally embolized minipig achieved creatinine clearance of 76–105 mL/min/m².
results.detail: Subtotal embolization spared the upper pole of the left kidney, which showed compensatory hypertrophy at necropsy. The implanted device used an external saline recirculation circuit, and the animal continued to receive standard hemodialysis.
results.quote: Creatinine and urea clearance through the SNMHD were 76–105 mL/min/m 2  and 140–165 mL/min/m 2 , respectively, without albumin leakage.

results.finding: In whole bovine blood tests with three samples, the membrane cast from 17.5% PES had the highest water filtration coefficient among the formulations tested.
results.detail: The single-layer screen used defibrinated whole bovine blood at 100 mL/min for 100 min at 200 mmHg. Follow-up tests used peristaltic circulation at 130 mmHg inlet pressure. Heparin priming was reported for the separate rat tests.
results.quote: The PES membrane formed from the casting solution with a PES concentration of 17.5% had the highest filtration coefficient among all the membranes.

results.finding: PEG-coated silicon nanopore hemofilter tested with bovine whole blood (triplicate experiments) had an albumin sieving coefficient of 0.07±0.03.
results.detail: The methods report triplicate experiments overall and leave the albumin-specific sample count unspecified.
results.quote: The observed sieving coefficient for albumin with bovine blood was 0.07±0.03, which closely matches the Ficoll results when the albumin size is calculated as the Stokes-Einstein diameter plus the thickness of the surrounding electrical double layer.

results.finding: A pump-free cell-free hemofilter tested in 3 beagles yielded up to 9.71 mL of filtrate during short ex vivo runs.
results.detail: The maximum is the sum of the six collection intervals in Table 2 for one dog. The daily rate is an extrapolation from that run.

results.finding: The implanted bioartificial kidney prototype in one mini-pig produced ultrafiltrate at 0.28 µL/min at explant.
results.detail: The daily equivalent extrapolates a single flow measurement at explant. The study did not measure 24-hour filtrate output.
results.quote: Ultrafiltrate was noted at both implant and explant, with a flow rate of 0.28 uL/min measured at explant.

results.finding: Implanted cell-free filters in 10 adult dogs with intact kidneys yielded initial ultrafiltration of 25.2 ± 6.4 mL/h (n=9 analyzed).
results.detail: The authors attributed declining output to clotting that blocked peripheral hollow fibers. Four of five dogs died from bleeding after one-stage surgery, while no bleeding deaths occurred in the five dogs that underwent two-stage surgery.
results.quote:
Just after implantation, ultrafilt-
rate obtained was 25.2±6.4ml/hour
in the average.

results.finding: A cell-free polyethersulfone filter maintained a nearly constant filtration coefficient over 5 hours in renal-artery-ligated rats, with three experiments per device configuration.
results.detail: The results call the rats nephrectomized, while the methods describe renal artery ligation to stop renal blood flow. The methods leave the specified anephric model unverified.
results.quote:
The filtration coefficient remained almost constant over 5 h of experiments as shown in Figure
6
C.

results.finding: In swine, 8 of 10 modified hemofilter implants remained patent for up to 26 days.
results.detail: Patency was assessed by physical exam, Doppler ultrasound, and fluoroscopy. The abstract does not identify the cause of lost patency or establish that patent filters were free of clotting.
results.quote: 80% patency (8/10) up to 26 days' duration.

results.finding: Implanted cell-free hollow-fiber filters in 10 dogs yielded 4 mL/h at the last follow-up.
results.detail: The last measurement was at 192 hours. The authors attributed declining output to clotting that blocked peripheral hollow fibers despite continuous heparin.
results.quote: 4ml/hour at 192 hours.

case_label = "Design". Reason: The implant design determines whether fluid and solute transport depend on living cells.

definition = "A manufactured system implanted wholly inside the body continuously removes wastes and excess water and regulates salts well enough to replace maintenance dialysis in chronic kidney failure. In one design, a blood filter produces a fluid containing water, salts and dissolved wastes. Living kidney cells return much of the filtered water to the blood, and the concentrated waste fluid drains to the bladder. Other designs use cell-free components to regulate salts and water.". Reason: Explaining what happens to the filtrate makes clear how an implant can remove wastes without losing the whole filtered volume.

goal.need = "On March 31, 2025, 516,837 people in the United States were on dialysis. For the 433,396 receiving in-center hemodialysis, a usual schedule was about four hours three times a week, plus travel. Home hemodialysis offers more flexibility but still takes hours on a machine. An implant that maintained waste clearance and fluid balance could free that time for work and family, whether someone was waiting for a donor kidney or needed long-term treatment. Some recipients could still need hormone replacement.". Reason: The dialysis census and treatment schedule identify who faces the burden and how much time an implant could return to them.

add statement by European Innovation Council, Horizon Europe KIDNEW project, 2023: "the KIDNEW project proposes to develop an implantable bioartificial kidney". Reason: The KIDNEW grant documents a European programme with an explicit implantable bioartificial kidney objective.
add case "Bioartificial". Reason: The Kidney Project's implant combines a manufactured filter with a living renal-cell bioreactor.
add case "Cell-free". Reason: The KidneyX cell-free design uses physical separation processes to perform functions that a bioartificial implant assigns to living cells.

add milestone after None: "A prototype implant component demonstrates its intended kidney function in the laboratory.". Reason: A measured laboratory demonstration marks progress before a filter can produce a clinically relevant daily volume.

edit m1: title = "An artificial-kidney blood filter produces at least 40 L/day of filtrate without clotting."; criterion = "Connect the filter to the circulation, with or without a pump. It must produce at least 40 L of filtrate per day without clotting, retain essential blood proteins such as albumin, and freely pass electrolytes and toxins that are not bound to proteins."; set_by = "Kidney Health Initiative, 2018 roadmap, Table 2, page 19, and Table 3, page 22."; threshold_quote = "Generates a filtrate of at least 40L/day"; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7]. Reason: The roadmap specifies a minimum filtrate volume and allows circulation with or without a pump, while the existing criterion includes animal results.

add milestone after m1: "A tubular component permits net reabsorption of 90%–95% of filtered volume outside the body.". Reason: The roadmap tests recovery of filtered water separately from production of filtrate, a distinction missing from the component milestones.

edit m2: criterion = "Demonstrate blood filtration by the candidate filter in a full-scale animal model that retains native kidney function. The need for the study and its duration depend on the product."; threshold_quote = "full-scale animal model with residual kidney function"; threshold_ref = 25; refs = [7, 25]. Reason: The criterion now tests filtration in the specified animal model without treating survival of isolated bioreactor cells as a filtration result.

add milestone after m2: "An integrated implant prototype demonstrates blood filtration and processing of the filtrate.". Reason: The integrated pig prototype tested filtration and subsequent fluid processing together, an achievement the filter-only milestones cannot record.

edit m3: criterion = "Demonstrate blood filtration by the candidate filter in an anephric animal model, with no residual native kidney function. The need for the study and its duration depend on the product."; threshold_quote = "anephric animal models without residual kidney function"; threshold_ref = 25; refs = [7, 25]. Reason: The roadmap specifies an anephric model, which is a more precise condition than severe renal impairment.

edit m4: criterion = "Demonstrate 12\u201324 months of continuous performance by a size-selective filter capable of producing 40 L of filtrate per day without clotting."; threshold_quote = "40L/day filtrate with 12\u201324 months of continuous performance"; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7]. Reason: The roadmap supplies a continuous filter-performance target independent of the duration of any published animal experiment.

edit m5: criterion = "Use a fully implanted artificial kidney in an authorized early feasibility study in people and obtain initial data on clinical safety and device function."; threshold_quote = "initial clinical safety and device functionality"; threshold_ref = 11; refs = [11]. Reason: The developer's dated trial status obscures the FDA test for an early feasibility study.

edit m6: criterion = "Complete a pivotal human investigation of the implanted system for its intended use as a replacement for maintenance dialysis. Evaluate safety and effectiveness against the study's prospectively specified primary endpoints."; threshold_quote = "A definitive study during which evidence is gathered to support the safety and effectiveness evaluation of the medical device for its intended use."; threshold_ref = 12; refs = [12]. Reason: The pivotal-study criterion can state what a completed study must evaluate without repeating the search for an implant-specific protocol.
